title: VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP on the same table

screens.prompt: In B7, return the unit price for the SKU typed in B6 using the table A1:C5.

hints.syntax: =VLOOKUP(B6,A2:C5,3,FALSE): table, then column, then the match flag.
hints.func-vlookup: VLOOKUP is this screen's function; XLOOKUP gets the next one.
hints.exact-match: The SKU list is in no useful order, so FALSE is required. Left out, Excel approximates and returns a neighbouring price.
hints.require-ref: Take the SKU from B6, so another product is one cell away.
hints.value: Count from the SKU column: product is 2, price is 3. Column 2 would return Clamp.
hints.error: #N/A is a SKU the table does not hold. #REF! is a column number wider than A2:C5.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing is looked up
no fourth argument, so the match falls back to approximate on an unsorted column
approximate match on a column of SKU codes
column 2 is the product name, not the price
the right answer by the other function; XLOOKUP gets its own screen
the table stops one column short, so the column number runs off the edge
the SKU typed into the formula, so a change in B6 never reaches the answer

screens.prompt: In B7, return the same unit price with XLOOKUP instead: the SKU in B6, the SKU column, the price column.

hints.syntax: =XLOOKUP(B6,A2:A5,C2:C5): search column, then answer column, with no number between them.
hints.func-xlookup: Same table, two ranges. There is no column to count and nothing to break when the sheet is reordered.
hints.require-ref: B6 again, so both screens answer the same question.
hints.value: The answer sits in the third argument, on the row where the match was found.
hints.error: A SKU outside A2:A5 gives #N/A, exactly as VLOOKUP would.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing is looked up
the right price by the older function; this screen is the XLOOKUP version
the same price built from two functions; this screen is the one-function version
returns the product name rather than the price
returns an empty column, so the price comes back as zero
the SKU typed into the formula, so a change in B6 never reaches the answer
adding a division by zero to the price returns #DIV/0!

docs.explain:
Both functions take the SKU in B6, which is CX-330, and return the price beside it. VLOOKUP wants the whole table A2:C5 plus a column number: 3 counts SKU, product, price and lands on 3.8. That number only means price while the table starts at column A.

XLOOKUP names its two columns instead, A2:A5 to search and C2:C5 to return. Insert a column, move the price, and the formula still points at the price.

The fourth argument in VLOOKUP is the one that gets forgotten. FALSE makes a near miss fail rather than pass, and on a column of SKU codes a near miss is another product at another price.

errors.text: The SKU is not in the searched column: a missing product, not a broken formula.
VLOOKUP's column number is wider than the table, which asks for a column the table does not have.

docs.atWork: A supplier price list pasted into a sheet, where the SKU column is the only reliable key.
docs.outcome: Read a price with either lookup and know which argument does which job.
docs.teaches: VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP side by side

seo.title: VLOOKUP vs XLOOKUP on the same table
seo.description: VLOOKUP counts columns from the table left edge. XLOOKUP names the searched and returned columns, so nothing is miscounted. Both want an exact match.
